story_review.one_viewing_summary: A generic drone launches from a dock at an industrial yard. A software screen displays an attributed anomaly alert. An illustrated letter receives date and approval stamps for periodic methane screening. The drone follows a route and supplies illustrative infrared footage. A person marks the plume, confirms it and triggers follow-up inspection. The film then exposes the protocol's limited AI wording, distinguishes a separate delayed reporting program and its proposed rescission, and closes on human confirmation beside an empty AI box.
story_review.opening_to_ending: The opening establishes the drone as the collecting machine. The middle shows that recognizable footage reaches a human reviewer, who marks and confirms its plume. The ending answers the question about who confirms the leak and retains the unknown AI contribution. It depicts neither a measured Permian leak nor an eventual repair.
story_review.weakest_transition: The 38.2 to 38.6 second handoff from the protocol title to the separate reporting program is the largest conceptual departure from the drone-review chain. The explicit separate-program disclosure and the removal of the drone prevent it from being presented as the same approval, although this remains the least direct causal connection.
